summary: Texas needs steadier gains on the ground to keep its passing options open against Ohio State. Watch the left side of the offensive line, the relief carries, and whether the defense can take the ball away without losing its assignments.

items.headline: Cooper suited up for practice, per On Texas Football
items.tldr: Thursday’s episode notes are newer than Monday’s report that he would miss Ohio State. A practice appearance does not confirm game clearance; watch for the final availability update.

items.headline: Texas gave up seven non-sack tackles for loss in the opener
items.tldr: Watch whether the left-guard rotation can help turn early-down runs into manageable gains. The important improvement is fewer wasted plays, even when the explosive run is not there.

items.headline: Biles forced a fumble and intercepted a screen in his Texas debut
items.tldr: Watch his recognition underneath as well as his pass rush. Staying with a receiver or reading a screen can be as valuable as chasing the quarterback.

items.headline: Manning connected with eight receivers in the opener
items.tldr: If Ohio State takes away the first read, watch whether Manning can find another option without holding the ball too long. Receiver balance matters most when the pocket gets crowded.

items.headline: DKR’s interactive map marks gates, water and first aid
items.tldr: Open the map before leaving for the stadium and pick your entrance. The launch announcement describes step-by-step wayfinding as a future feature.

lead.headline: Make the ordinary run work.
lead.body: Watch the blocking on early downs. Consistent gains would let Texas use its receivers without asking the pocket to survive obvious passing situations.

matchup.question: What would put Texas in control?
matchup.answer: Turn early-down runs into useful gains, then make Ohio State defend the full passing game. On defense, keep eyes on the ball without abandoning coverage.

signals.title: Run blocking
signals.detail: Watch whether the guards and tackles stay connected against movement. A modest gain keeps more options available than a tackle for loss.
signals.prompt: What should I watch in the Texas run game?

signals.title: Passing options
signals.detail: If the first receiver is covered, watch how quickly Manning moves on. The throw underneath can keep the drive alive.
signals.prompt: How can Texas keep its passing game balanced?

signals.title: Ball recognition
signals.detail: Watch whether the linebackers recognize screens while staying disciplined against the run. A pass rush only helps if the ball has nowhere easy to go.
signals.prompt: What should I watch from Texas’s linebackers?

signals.title: Relief carries
signals.detail: Watch the reserve back’s protection and ball security when he enters. Keeping the offense on schedule matters more than forcing a highlight run.
signals.prompt: Who should I watch behind Texas’s lead backs?
